questions.problem: Let $a=⟨-2,-1,-4⟩$ and $b=⟨6,-5,3⟩.$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{(-2)\cdot 6+(-1)\cdot (-5)+(-4)\cdot 3}{{6}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{3}^{2}}b \\  & =-\frac{19}{70}⟨6,-5,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{57}{35},\frac{19}{14},-\frac{57}{70}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $p=⟨1,-1,1⟩$ and $q=⟨8,4,2⟩.$ Find the vector projection of $q$ onto $p.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{p}\,q & =\frac{p\cdot q}{p\cdot p}p \\  & =\frac{{p}_{x}{q}_{x}+{p}_{y}{q}_{y}+{p}_{z}{q}_{z}}{{p}_{x}^{2}+{p}_{y}^{2}+{p}_{z}^{2}}p \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 8+(-1)\cdot 4+1\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}p \\  & =\frac{6}{3}⟨1,-1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-2,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $a=⟨2,-1,-2⟩$ and $b=⟨x,-4,0⟩.$ Given that the projection of $a$ onto $b$ is the zero vector, find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =2\cdot x+(-1)\cdot (-4)+(-2)\cdot 0 \\  & =2x+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 2x+4 & =0 \\ 2x & =-4 \\ x & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
